latencies.notes: L1D-hit load. The bare pointer chase ldptr.d $r4, $r4, 0 measures 3.97 cycles, so the load latency is 4; adding add.d reads 5.97, one cycle more than the add itself, which is the ALU consumer path (5).

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: ldptr.d $r12, $r20, 0; ldptr.d $r13, $r20, 8; ldptr.d $r14, $r20, 16; ldptr.d $r15, $r20, 24; ldptr.d $r16, $r20, 32; ldptr.d $r17, $r20, 40; ldptr.d $r18, $r20, 48; ldptr.d $r19, $r20, 56
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024' --asm 'ldptr.d $r12, $r20, 0; ldptr.d $r13, $r20, 8; ldptr.d $r14, $r20, 16; ldptr.d $r15, $r20, 24; ldptr.d $r16, $r20, 32; ldptr.d $r17, $r20, 40; ldptr.d $r18, $r20, 48; ldptr.d $r19, $r20, 56'

notes: 4 cycles, the same for every width and for both the base and the index or bound operand. The load result is available four cycles after the address, and a chain that passes it through an ALU operation before using it as the next address reads one cycle more than that operation, which is what the address generator charges for an ALU-produced address rather than load latency.
